```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  eval = FALSE
)
```

[Choosing a results generator](https://cfbseedR.sportsdataverse.org/articles/results-generators.html)
introduces `cfbseedR_ratings_compute_results()` on toy data. This article
feeds it real ratings from [cfbfastR](https://cfbfastR.sportsdataverse.org/)
and reports how every generator did on real seasons. The code needs network
access (and, for the CollegeFootballData endpoints, a `CFBD_API_KEY`), so it
is shown but not run here.

```{r setup}
library(cfbseedR)
library(dplyr)

season <- 2026
sched <- cfbfastR::load_cfb_schedules(season)
games <- cfb_games_from_schedule(sched)
teams <- unique(data.frame(
  team = c(sched$home_team, sched$away_team),
  conference = c(sched$home_conference, sched$away_conference)
))
```

The `ratings` table needs `team` (spelled as in `games`), `rating` and,
ideally, `games`: the number of games behind each rating, which picks the
games-played bucket of `scale` and `margin_sd`. The fit counted FBS-vs-FBS
games; counting every completed game, as here, is close enough for a
bucket:

```{r games-played}
played <- games |>
  filter(!is.na(result)) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(home_team, away_team), values_to = "team") |>
  count(team, name = "games")
```

## Starting ELO ratings for the default generator

The default generator's results below were measured on CollegeFootballData's
pregame ELO, which carries over between seasons. Pass it as `elo` to start the
simulation from it (at the start of the season the rating from each team's
opening game; mid-season, the rating as of the current week):

```{r elo}
elo <- cfbfastR::cfbd_ratings_elo(year = season, preseason = TRUE)
start <- setNames(rep(1500, nrow(teams)), teams$team) # FCS teams and any gaps
known <- elo$team %in% teams$team
start[elo$team[known]] <- elo$elo[known]

sim_elo <- cfb_simulations(games, teams, elo = start, simulations = 10000)
```

Every team in `teams` needs a starting value; one left out would start at
`NA`.

## Points ratings

Any rating in points per game against an average team works with
`rating_type = "points"`. SP+ and FPI both come through cfbfastR:

```{r points}
sp <- cfbfastR::cfbd_ratings_sp(year = season) |>
  filter(team != "nationalAverages") |>
  select(team, rating) |>
  left_join(played, by = "team")

fpi <- cfbfastR::cfbd_ratings_fpi(year = season) |>
  transmute(team, rating = fpi) |>
  left_join(played, by = "team")

sim_sp <- cfb_simulations(
  games, teams,
  compute_results = cfbseedR_ratings_compute_results,
  ratings = sp, rating_type = "points",
  simulations = 10000
)
```

The default `scale` for points is close to 1 (1.03 averaged over the
season), so a published points rating maps almost one to one onto the
expected margin. The fitted values are a little below 1 for ratings built on
4-5 games and a little above it for 0-3 and 8+, which is noise around 1
rather than a trend.

## Adjusted EPA per play

`rating_type = "adj_epa"` takes an opponent-adjusted net EPA per play:
offensive EPA/play minus defensive EPA/play allowed. Its defaults are
sportsdataverse-py's modern-era pregame-prediction constants, fitted to that
package's `adj_net` (from `cfb_ratings()` in Python), which is the natural
input.

From R, CollegeFootballData's opponent-adjusted team EPA is one source:

```{r adj-epa}
adj <- cfbfastR::cfbd_metrics_wepa_team_season(year = season) |>
  transmute(team, rating = epa_total - epa_allowed_total) |>
  left_join(played, by = "team")

sim_adj <- cfb_simulations(
  games, teams,
  compute_results = cfbseedR_ratings_compute_results,
  ratings = adj, rating_type = "adj_epa",
  simulations = 10000
)
```

That is a different opponent adjustment from sportsdataverse-py's, so its
spread across teams can differ. Compare `sd(adj$rating)` with the spread of
the ratings you trust; if they differ a lot, pass your own `scale` (a fit of
this package's fitting script's own adjustment gave 59 / 54 / 61 / 63
points per EPA/play by bucket, against the shipped 32 / 38 / 45 / 50; see the
[fit record](https://github.com/sportsdataverse/cfbseedR/blob/main/data-raw/cfb_generator_constants.md)).

## Raw EPA per play

`rating_type = "raw_epa"` takes net EPA per play with no opponent
adjustment, built from cfbfastR play-by-play. The fitted defaults used pass
and rush plays, dropped kneel-downs, and dropped garbage time (a score margin
above 43, 37, 27 and 21 points in quarters 1 to 4; the quarter-4 value also
covers overtime):

```{r raw-epa}
pbp <- cfbfastR::load_cfb_pbp(season)
garbage <- c(43, 37, 27, 21)

plays <- pbp |>
  filter(
    pass == 1 | rush == 1, !is.na(EPA),
    !grepl("kneel", play_text, ignore.case = TRUE),
    is.na(pos_score_diff_start) |
      abs(pos_score_diff_start) <= garbage[pmin(pmax(period, 1), 4)]
  )

raw <- full_join(
  plays |> group_by(team = pos_team) |> summarise(off = mean(EPA)),
  plays |> group_by(team = def_pos_team) |> summarise(def = mean(EPA)),
  by = "team"
) |>
  transmute(team, rating = off - def) |>
  left_join(played, by = "team")

sim_raw <- cfb_simulations(
  games, teams,
  compute_results = cfbseedR_ratings_compute_results,
  ratings = raw, rating_type = "raw_epa",
  simulations = 10000
)
```

Restrict `plays` to FBS-vs-FBS games if you want the ratings on exactly the
footing of the fit.

## How the generators compared

[`data-raw/cfb_generator_constants.R`](https://github.com/sportsdataverse/cfbseedR/blob/main/data-raw/cfb_generator_constants.R)
scored every generator walk-forward on
FBS-vs-FBS games from 2014-2025 (2020 left out): a game in week `w` was
predicted from ratings built only on games before week `w`, from week 4 on
and in the postseason, once both teams had at least two prior games. That
is 6,854 games. The ratings generators' coefficients were fitted with the
test season left out. The ELO row is the shipped ELO margin formula fed with
CollegeFootballData's pregame ELO, whose constants were fitted on all
seasons, a slight edge for ELO. Intervals are paired differences against
ELO, bootstrapped over (season, week) clusters. Every prediction is one week
ahead: ratings are refreshed with each week's real results.

| Generator | Mean absolute error | vs ELO [95% interval] | Brier score of the home win | vs ELO [95% interval] |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ELO (default) | 12.94 | - | 0.1875 | - |
| points | 13.10 | +0.16 [+0.02, +0.31] | 0.1910 | +0.0035 [+0.0007, +0.0065] |
| adjusted EPA/play | 13.38 | +0.44 [+0.27, +0.60] | 0.1969 | +0.0094 [+0.0059, +0.0130] |
| raw EPA/play | 13.70 | +0.76 [+0.59, +0.94] | 0.2017 | +0.0142 [+0.0105, +0.0179] |

By the games played behind the weaker of the two ratings (mean absolute
error):

| Games | Games scored | ELO | points | adjusted EPA | raw EPA |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-3 | 1,387 | **12.73** | 13.39 | 13.75 | 14.13 |
| 4-5 | 1,428 | **12.85** | 13.19 | 13.32 | 13.48 |
| 6-7 | 1,412 | 13.05 | **13.03** | 13.21 | 13.56 |
| 8-20 | 2,627 | 13.04 | **12.93** | 13.30 | 13.68 |

ELO wins early because that ELO carries each team's rating over from the
previous season; the other ratings are current-season only. From about six
games on, the points rating is level with it (the differences in the last
two rows are within the test's noise). Hence the advice: keep the default
ELO generator, with carried-over `elo` starting ratings, for a full-season
simulation, and consider a points rating for the last weeks of a season or
for the postseason. Postseason games were scored together with the late
regular season, not on their own.

The adjusted-EPA rows score the fitting script's own adjustment with its own
coefficients, not sportsdataverse-py's `adj_net` with the shipped defaults,
which this test does not score.
